steps: The cell membrane separates the contents of the cell from its surroundings.
It is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
items.finalAnswer: The cell membrane separates the cell from its surroundings and controls the movement of substances into and out of it.

steps: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids.
It transports these materials to other parts of the cell or outside the cell.
items.finalAnswer: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids for transport.

steps: They digest foreign materials, food particles and worn-out cell parts.
items.finalAnswer: Lysosomes digest foreign materials, food particles and worn-out cell parts.

steps: Peroxisomes detoxify harmful substances and break down lipids.
items.finalAnswer: Peroxisomes detoxify harmful substances and break down lipids.

steps: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids.
It also helps in detoxifying harmful substances.
items.finalAnswer: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids and helps detoxify harmful substances.

steps: Plant cells usually have one large central vacuole, while animal cells have smaller vacuoles, often several.
The large plant vacuole stores water and other substances and helps maintain the cell's shape.
items.finalAnswer: Plant cells usually have one large central vacuole, whereas animal cells have smaller vacuoles, often several.

steps: If lysosomal enzymes stop working, materials that should be digested may accumulate inside the cell.
This can interfere with cell functioning and may eventually cause cell damage or death.
items.finalAnswer: Undigested materials may accumulate, disrupting cell function and potentially causing cell damage or death.

steps: Cristae are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
They increase the membrane's surface area, providing more space for the reactions that produce ATP during cellular respiration.
items.finalAnswer: Cristae increase the inner membrane's surface area for ATP-producing reactions in cellular respiration.
